column1: Putting the Pieces Together According to the Mundell–Fleming model, a small open economy with perfect capital mobility can be described by two equations: Y 5 C (Y 2 T)  I (r∗)  G  NX (e) IS∗, M/P 5 L (r∗, Y ) LM∗. The first equation describes equilibrium in the goods market; the second describes equilibrium in the money market. The exogenous variables are fiscal policy G and T, monetary policy M, the price level P, and the world interest rate r∗. The endogenous variables are income Y and the exchange rate e.
